question.text: Two simple harmonic waves having equal amplitudes of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and equal frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> are moving along the same direction. The resultant amplitude is also <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The phase difference between the individual waves is _____ degree.

solution.text:
If two waves have the same amplitude, frequency, and direction, but are out of phase by ϕ degrees, then the amplitude of the resultant waves is given by AR=2AcosΔϕ2

Here, A1=A2=AR=8 cm

So, cosΔϕ2=12

Or phase difference between the individual waves is Δϕ2=60°⇒Δϕ=120°.
